name: Hyam
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: John, Philip Hayab. 2016. Basic Hyam Grammar with Ethnographic Notes (not found online). NOTE: Blench 2006 ''You couldn't make it up' - the phonology of Hyam' WAS read (rogerblench.info via Wayback): it describes three level tones plus glides but contains no stress statement.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2006. 'You couldn't make it up': the phonology of Hyam. Draft circulated for comment, Mallam Dendo, Cambridge (printout 2 Jan 2006), 13 pp. [Hyam of Nok]
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 Phonology covers vowels, consonants and 3.3 Tones (p.10: 'Hyam has three level tones and rising and falling tones...'); the words stress/accent do not occur.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. Hyam of Nok web page (rogerblench.info, Wayback 2021) — index listing wordlist, phonology, consonant-alternation papers only.
sources.note: Index page only; confirms no further Hyam phonology documents were posted.

sources.citation: John, Philip Hayab. 2017. Narratives of identity and sociocultural worldview in song texts of the Ham of Nigeria: a discourse analysis investigation. PhD dissertation, Stellenbosch University, 361 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; only a remark (p.53) that kyom/kywom/kyóm are distinguished by 'the rise and fall of tonal disparities'. Cites Hayab 2016 Basic Hyam Grammar as the grammar of record.

sources.citation: Hayab, Philip. 2016. Hyam Literacy website: 'Vowels and Consonants in Hyam', 'Alphabet', 'Hyam language orthography and codification' (hyamliteracy.com, Wayback 2017 captures).
sources.note: Segment inventories only; 'stress' named once as something an orthography should regulate, no rule given; dialects said to differ in 'tonal variation'.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2010. A wordlist of the Hyam language of Nok in Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft, Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, Cambridge (printout 31 Aug 2010), 31 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; notes tone transcription is 'highly variable' and describes tone-raising plurals (Table 2).

sources.citation: Yaro, Mary James. 2010. A contrastive analysis of tense formation and usage in Jaba [Kanyi = Kwyeny dialect] and English language. MA thesis, Dept. of English, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria (Kubanni handle 123456789/1644).
sources.note: No word-stress statement for Jaba; states tone marks tense (falling tone = present, rising tone = past). 'Stress' appears only in discussion of English CONtract/conTRACT.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2006. Hyam consonant alternation. Draft circulated for comment, Cambridge, 12 Nov 2006, 15 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on Hyam stress. Sec. 2.4 'Stem tone' (p.3) says Hyam has more glide tones than level tones on monosyllabic morphemes; 'accent systems' mentioned only generically for Atlantic languages.
